newsitem.title: UK: New test catches asthma in young children.
newsitem.headline: New test catches asthma in young children.

text.p: British researchers said on Thursday they had devised a new test that can help tell whether very young children have asthma.
They said their sensor detects the amount of nitric oxide, the gas associated with the inflammation caused by asthma, in a child's breath.
"Until now, to accurately assess if a child under five has asthma has been very difficult," Jane Valente of the charity Action Research, who headed the study, said in a statement.
"The sensor is built into a face mask and consists of a small strip of paper containng chemicals that react to nitric oxide."
